POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation only to the extent it is attributable to a rider instruction, and a driver's own proposal is not a rider instruction, so the clause's limb (a) fails at the outset. With waypoint_hint null on that message, the clause's corroboration limb cannot be run either: POL-RD-04 is unavailable and the diversion is left wholly unexplained by anything the rider did.

The driver's entire defence is a traffic event on the BKE near Dairy Farm, and no advisory in the pool supports it. I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00102-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its issue detail records that no LTA advisory covers the BKE or the Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the 11:16-11:55 window. I rely on that absence itself, which is citable. POL-RD-03 exonerates a deviation only where a traffic_advisory names a road or expressway segment the optimal route traverses and carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached it; no such advisory exists here, so nothing on this record excuses the longer route.

Because the only defence pleaded is a traffic event asserted with no traffic_advisory anywhere in the pool - EV-ADVIS-00102-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and does not cover the trip window - POL-RD-10(5) is engaged: an exculpatory basis is asserted against an artifact that is not in the pool. Escalation is mandatory and terminal under that clause, and it holds the disputed SGD 7.00 rather than letting the present charged state stand, which is the only relief this record can give the rider. The full case summary, both briefs and the admissibility report should go to the reviewer.

I am straight about the arithmetic rather than stretching it: the fully unimpaired track - 193 fixes, 10 s sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps - puts the traced distance at 21.79 km against the 20.4 km optimal, an excess of 1.39 km, which is 6.81%. That excess is real and cleanly measured, but it falls short of POL-RD-01's 20% establishment limb, so no deviation is established on this record and I do not press a POL-RD-02 recomputation, which by its terms runs only on an established deviation. That is exactly why the rider's route here is escalation under POL-RD-10(5), which holds the money, rather than a partial refund.

The driver's congestion account cites no evidence ID at all - no advisory, no gantry, no artifact - and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver, and that assertions from either side citing no evidence ID carry no weight and are discarded. The rider's version, by contrast, is pinned to this trip's own artifacts: the trip record, the gps trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00102, so the identity requirement of POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied and this dispute is decided on this trip's evidence rather than on anyone's say-so.

The rider's route-deviation claim fails the governing establishment test. Measured the way POL-RD-01 requires - by the trace distance, 21.79 km, which the clause makes the governing field over the rounded trip_record copy of 21.8 km - against the booked optimal distance of 20.4 km, the excess is only 1.39 km. That is 6.81% of the optimal route, far below the 20% the clause demands, so the percentage limb fails and no deviation is established on this trip.

POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs of the test to pass: the excess must exceed 20% of optimal AND exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms. Only the absolute limb is even arguable here, and the platform's own derivation of this trace records the deviation status as 'no deviation'. Because the percentage limb fails, the establishment test as a whole fails and the rider cannot get past the threshold.

The measurement the rider must rely on is unimpaired and cannot be attacked. The trace carries 193 fixes at a steady 10-second sampling interval across the whole 32-minute trip, at 100% coverage, with no gaps, no jumps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. There is no basis to discount this measurement or to require corroboration from an independent source.

Where the establishment tests under POL-RD-01 fail, the clause directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00, so NO_ACTION simply leaves the metered charge standing exactly as it is - which is the correct outcome for the driver here.

ledger.claim: The only chat entry on this trip, MSG-00102-001 in the chat log, is a message from the DRIVER - 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?' - sent at 11:29:04, roughly six minutes after the vehicle had already been moving (started 11:23:30); the rider never replied, the message merely being read at 11:29:40. POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation only to the extent it is attributable to a rider instruction, and a driver's own proposal is not a rider instruction, so the clause's limb (a) fails at the outset. With waypoint_hint null on that message, the clause's corroboration limb cannot be run either: POL-RD-04 is unavailable and the diversion is left wholly unexplained by anything the rider did.

The driver's entire defence is a traffic event on the BKE near Dairy Farm, and no advisory in the pool supports it. I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00102-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its issue detail records that no LTA advisory covers the BKE or the Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the 11:16-11:55 window. I rely on that absence itself, which is citable. POL-RD-03 exonerates a deviation only where a traffic_advisory names a road or expressway segment the optimal route traverses and carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached it; no such advisory exists here, so nothing on this record excuses the longer route.

Because the only defence pleaded is a traffic event asserted with no traffic_advisory anywhere in the pool - EV-ADVIS-00102-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and does not cover the trip window - POL-RD-10(5) is engaged: an exculpatory basis is asserted against an artifact that is not in the pool. Escalation is mandatory and terminal under that clause, and it holds the disputed SGD 7.00 rather than letting the present charged state stand, which is the only relief this record can give the rider. The full case summary, both briefs and the admissibility report should go to the reviewer.

I am straight about the arithmetic rather than stretching it: the fully unimpaired track - 193 fixes, 10 s sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps - puts the traced distance at 21.79 km against the 20.4 km optimal, an excess of 1.39 km, which is 6.81%. That excess is real and cleanly measured, but it falls short of POL-RD-01's 20% establishment limb, so no deviation is established on this record and I do not press a POL-RD-02 recomputation, which by its terms runs only on an established deviation. The driver's congestion account cites no evidence ID at all - no advisory, no gantry, no artifact - and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver, and that assertions from either side citing no evidence ID carry no weight and are discarded. The rider's version, by contrast, is pinned to this trip's own artifacts: the trip record, the gps trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00102, so the identity requirement of POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied and this dispute is decided on this trip's evidence rather than on anyone's say-so.

The rider's route-deviation claim fails the governing establishment test.
